```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(coherentSurv)
```

This example follows synthetic participants for two years after randomized
baseline assignment. Hospitalizations and adverse-event episodes can recur
before death. We retain the complete sequence of observed intervals, then
estimate arm differences in expected counts, death risk and restricted mean
time alive. These invented event labels and rates illustrate the software;
they are not clinical evidence about a treatment.

## State the question before fitting

For each assigned arm, the outcomes are the number of each recurrent event
before death or year two, death by year two, and time alive through year two.
The population summary is the arm-one mean minus the arm-zero mean, using the
same baseline population for both arms. A participant who dies contributes
their observed recurrent events before death; they are not dropped from the
population.

```{r estimand}
trial_estimand <- list(
  population = "All synthetic participants eligible at randomization",
  treatment = "Baseline assignment 1 versus 0, maintained through two years",
  endpoint = c(
    "Hospitalization count before death or year two",
    "Adverse-event episode count before death or year two",
    "All-cause death by year two",
    "Restricted mean time alive through year two"
  ),
  intercurrent_events = paste(
    "Death ends recurrent-event accumulation.",
    "Independent loss to follow-up is right censoring.",
    "Switching and treatment discontinuation are not generated."
  ),
  population_summary = "Arm-one minus arm-zero standardized mean for each outcome"
)
trial_estimand
```

Death stopping event accumulation is a definition of these outcomes. It is
**not a while-on-treatment strategy**: treatment discontinuation is a separate
event that would need a protocol-specific definition and analysis. A lower
event count can also reflect earlier death, so interpret burden together with
death risk and time alive. Restricted mean time alive is not automatically
time free of hospitalization or toxicity.

The optional `estimand` argument preserves this declaration. It does not
change the implemented estimand or verify a protocol's identification or
regulatory requirements.

## Generate exact histories under randomized assignment

`cs_simulate()` draws its baseline variable `x` from Bernoulli(0.5). Here we
interpret that generated variable as randomized assignment and rename it
`assigned`; its supplied coefficients create treatment effects on the event
intensities. We use zero latent frailty and a declared count cap of one, so the
retained count state and assignment are sufficient under the generating law.
The cap limits the history summary in the intensity, not the number of events
that can accumulate. Independent loss to follow-up has rate 0.08 per year.

```{r generator}
simulate_trial <- function(n = 120L, horizon = 2, seed = 20261126L) {
  d <- cs_simulate(
    n = n, horizon = horizon,
    rates = c(.65, .40, .30),
    beta = c(-.25, -.20, -.15),
    history = c(.10, .10, .12),
    dispersion = 0, censor_rate = .08,
    history_cap = 1L, seed = seed, time_unit = "years"
  )
  d$assigned <- d$x
  d$x <- NULL
  d$event_type <- c("none", "hospitalization", "adverse_event")[d$event_type + 1L]
  d$censored <- as.integer(
    d$event_type == "none" & d$terminal == 0L & d$stop < horizon
  )
  d
}

trial <- simulate_trial()
head(trial, 6)

# One endpoint row per participant, used only for the cohort summary and OS extract.
endpoint <- trial[!duplicated(trial$id, fromLast = TRUE), ]
cohort_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(participants = rep(1L, nrow(endpoint)),
        deaths = endpoint$terminal, early_censoring = endpoint$censored),
  by = list(assigned = endpoint$assigned), FUN = sum
)
cohort_summary
```

An event row's `terminal` flag records death. The separate `censored` flag marks
an early loss-to-follow-up endpoint with no concurrent event; it is zero on
ordinary recurrent-event rows. Administrative follow-up at year two does not
need an early-censor indicator. All time variables use elapsed years from
randomization.

## Fit the baseline causal model

The formula `~1` declares no baseline confounder strata in this randomized
example. Treatment is supplied separately, with its known allocation
probability. The three cross-fitting folds contain whole participants, and
the log-linear nuisance model includes the declared retained count state.

```{r causal-fit}
fit <- cs_causal(
  formula = ~1, data = trial,
  treatment = "assigned", horizon = 2, censor = "censored",
  unit = "id", start = "start", stop = "stop",
  event_type = "event_type", terminal = "terminal",
  event_types = c("hospitalization", "adverse_event"),
  time_unit = "years", propensity = .5,
  spec = list(nfolds = 3L, history_cap = 1L,
              working = "loglinear", grid = 32L),
  seed = 41L, estimand = trial_estimand
)

contrasts <- cs_causal_contrast(fit, contrast = "difference", interval = "wald")
knitr::kable(contrasts, digits = 3)
```

The `arm0` and `arm1` columns are mean counts, death probabilities or years alive,
according to `target`. `estimate` is their difference. For each arm, a common
event-history law supplies all four outcomes, and death stops further recurrent
rewards. The arm contrast retains their joint influence-function covariance.
It is not obtained by interpreting a prognostic regression coefficient as a
causal effect. A burden contrast is a difference in expected counts, not a
difference in occurrence probabilities.

`wald` requests pointwise asymptotic limits. The package also provides a
simultaneous multiplier calculation over the regular contrast coordinates:

```{r simultaneous-intervals}
simultaneous <- cs_causal_contrast(
  fit, contrast = "difference", interval = "multiplier", draws = 300L, seed = 7L
)
knitr::kable(simultaneous[c("target", "estimate", "lower", "upper",
                           "inference_status")], digits = 3)
fit$convergence
fit$diagnostics
```

Inspect `inference_status` for every outcome. A failed score, zero-event boundary
or invalid variance can leave limits undefined (`NA`); keep that result visible.
Neither interval construction promises finite-sample coverage for this small
synthetic trial. The interpolation diagnostic concerns numerical approximation,
not sampling uncertainty; a substantive analysis should also examine grid
refinement.

Identification requires consistency, no interference, positive treatment
probabilities and conditionally independent censoring. Randomization and
independent censoring hold by construction here. The model also requires a
sufficient retained state. Influence-function inference additionally requires
regular targeting and appropriate nuisance convergence; this example establishes
neither universal efficiency nor validity under latent-history misspecification.
`cs_causal()` does not implement switching treatments, dynamic policies or
automatic coarsened causal histories.

## Map a separate ADTTE-style overall-survival extract

Recurrent histories and a selected time-to-first/absorbing endpoint are different
data products. The following artificial extract contains exactly one overall-
survival (`OS`) row per participant. For this extract we explicitly define
`CNSR = 0` as death, `1` as administrative censoring and `2` as early loss to
follow-up. These code meanings are local declarations, not inferred conventions.

```{r adam-mapping}
adtte <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = sprintf("S%03d", endpoint$id),
  PARAMCD = "OS", AVAL = endpoint$stop, AVALU = "years",
  CNSR = ifelse(endpoint$terminal == 1L, 0L,
                ifelse(endpoint$censored == 1L, 2L, 1L))
)
adsl <- data.frame(USUBJID = adtte$USUBJID, assigned = endpoint$assigned)

os_history <- cs_from_adam(
  adtte = adtte, paramcd = "OS", event_codes = 0L, censor_codes = c(1L, 2L),
  time_unit = "years",
  duration_definition = "Exact elapsed years from randomization to death or observation end",
  ascertainment = "Complete synthetic death ascertainment until the recorded observation end",
  provenance = "Synthetic OS extract derived from simulate_trial(), seed 20261126",
  adsl = adsl, covariates = "assigned"
)
stopifnot(identical(os_history$terminal, as.integer(endpoint$terminal)))
table(CNSR = adtte$CNSR, terminal = os_history$terminal)
head(os_history[c("id", "start", "stop", "terminal", "assigned")])
```

The mapping uses membership in `event_codes`; `1 - CNSR` would incorrectly
produce a negative event indicator for code 2. `CNSR` describes this selected
participant endpoint, not censoring at each recurrent-event row. The mapper
does not reconstruct recurrence, accept repeated ADTTE rows as a complete event
history, or certify CDISC compliance. The causal fit above used the original
interval histories, not this reduced OS extract.

## Retain the declaration and audit information

```{r audit}
report <- cs_audit_report(fit, include_session = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(report$model$estimand_declaration, trial_estimand))
report$model$estimand_declaration
report$fit_context$data_fingerprint$algorithm
report$convergence

audit_json <- cs_audit_report(fit, format = "json", include_session = FALSE)
stopifnot(jsonlite::validate(audit_json))
attr(os_history, "cs_mapping")[c("paramcd", "event_codes", "censor_codes", "scope")]
```

The report preserves the analyst declaration, fit diagnostics and a fingerprint
of serialized input data. It supports traceability; it does not establish causal
assumptions, protocol compliance, electronic-signature controls or an immutable
audit trail. Source mappings, outcome definitions and the analysis plan still
require study-specific review.
